relevance_note: Case series of three Indian families with Blau syndrome and NOD2 variants described individually, e.g. 'Clinical exome sequencing for the index case showed heterozygous mutation at the NOD2 gene'.
method_note: Rows written by hand from reading the paper (a Research Square preprint version); a short Python script only assembled the JSON and checked spans. Probands are called only 'Proband' (a role word), so they are labelled 'unnamed person k' in order of first mention and relatives are labelled relative to them. Variant strings are kept as printed in the Markdown, including the HTML entity '>' for '>' and the missing dot in 'c 1324C > T'. Family 1: the text gives the mother as homozygous and the proband and younger sister as heterozygous for the same variant; recorded as printed. Family 2: the sentence 'clinical exome sequence was sent for both the index case and the mother. It showed NOD2 mutation...' does not say explicitly that the mother carries it; Table 1 ('F2 - E383K ( proband mother )') does, so the mother has a variant row and the proband's inheritance is 'inherited maternal' from that cell. Family 2 'One of the other twin female babies' with nail dystrophy is included as an affected relative (unnamed person 3) whose exact relation to the proband is not stated; no variant row. Family 3 mother has uveitis but no genetic testing is reported; no variant row. Family 3 proband: 'presented ... with inflammatory polyarthritis' and on examination 'no active arthritis'; read as history versus examination, not a contradiction, so arthritis is observed and 'active arthritis on examination' excluded. Family 1 mother: uveitis taken from the Discussion ('uveitis in only the mother'), while the case text says 'recurrent redness of the eyes', 'probable uveitis' and an unremarkable ophthalmological examination; the unremarkable examination is recorded as written (D-27: a whole examination excludes nothing more specific). The same Discussion sentence names the first family's three members, so uveitis is excluded for the younger sister by group statement. Camptodactyly for the Family 1 mother rests on 'flexion contracture, suggestive of camptodactyly' (hedged). Normal ESR alone does not exclude the composite checklist item 'elevated inflammatory markers (ESR/CRP)', left not reported. Discussion statements that do not name a person were not attributed: 'one patient had bilateral amblyopia, allergic conjunctivitis and recurrent intermediate uveitis' (mixes features from different case descriptions), 'Another patient had recurrent uveitis and vitritis with complications like cataract', 'In family 2, one patient showed ... pleural effusion with patchy consolidation', 'one patient presented with camptodactyly with wrist deformity and one had finger flexion deformity'. Literature patients included under the v4 rule: Ukae et al (7) Japanese girl (pre-school sarcoidosis, with features) and the Saini and Rose (11) patient (familial granulomatous synovitis, hepatic granulomas). Table 1 gives only study-level counts for other series and yields no rows. n_patients_reported and cohort_size_as_stated use '7 patients in 3 families' from Table 1, which counts the untested Family 3 mother; year is the preprint posting date.
